Sessions & context

A saved session is a transcript on disk. Context is the material the model can use for its next reply. Resetting one does not always mean deleting the other.

Reset context, keep history. Starting a new chat clears the active model context while leaving saved sessions on disk. Permanent deletion is a separate, explicit action.

Manage saved sessions

Desktop: choose New chat to start fresh, or open Chats to search and resume saved conversations. A session is saved after its first message.

  • Open a row to resume it; double-click its title to rename it.
  • Use the row menu to edit tags, pin, archive, export JSON, or continue in the terminal.
  • Archive removes a chat from the active list but keeps it on disk; choose Restore to bring it back.
  • Delete asks for a second click. It is permanent and never auto-approved.

The desktop's Where you left off digest is generated locally from the saved session, makes no model call, and does not populate the model cache. It stays hidden during streaming and can be dismissed for that session.

Terminal session commands

Run /session for the manager, or use an action directly. Opening accepts a unique session-ID prefix.

/session
/session list
/session open 20261118
/session rename Release notes
/session pin
/session delete 20261118 confirm

list also accepts ls; open accepts load. Deletion requires confirm, yes, or --yes after the target ID. Without that word, the command only shows what would be deleted.

The launcher can also resume a saved chat with dizel --session <session-id>. See moving a chat between clients for the desktop handoff.

Reset versus clear

ActionVisible transcriptModel contextSaved sessions
/resetClearedClearedKept
/clearClearedKeptKept
/session delete … confirmRemoved if currentCurrent session replacedTarget permanently deleted

/reset asks for confirmation; /reset force, yes, or -y bypasses that prompt. Use /clear only when you want a clean workspace without making the model forget the conversation.

Read the context panel

The desktop context panel counts the active system prompt, project context, conversation, and reserved reply space on the server with the model's tokenizer. In the terminal, /context reports current tokens, capacity, and the allocated reply budget.

The usage meter is different: it uses a policy estimate to meter a provider's 12-hour bucket. Its percentage is not an exact tokenizer count and is not the vendor's billing total.

  • Routine trimming drops the oldest eligible turns when the model's real context budget is exceeded, preserving recent messages and protected attachment/tool context.
  • Usage compaction starts at 84% of the active provider's policy bucket. It replaces older turns with a short extractive summary and keeps the latest four messages; it makes no model call.
  • Each provider window permits five compactions. After that, start a new chat or wait for the 12-hour window to reset.
/context

Project rules and durable memory

At the project root, DIZEL.md and AGENTS.md are loaded into the system prompt. Their combined input is capped at 12,000 characters. Keep durable instructions there rather than repeating them in every chat.

Project memory is separate: it is keyed by the resolved project path and stored in the app data directory, not written into your repository. Dizel injects up to 6,000 characters of memory into the system prompt. Treat every saved entry as visible to the model.

/memory
/memory rules
/memory add Uses CRLF for .cmd files
/memory remove <id-or-index>
/memory clear

Where the data lives

By default, sessions are JSON files under data/history, and project memory is under data/memory. Packaged builds can point history at Electron's user-data directory. Set DIZEL_DATA_DIR to override the shared data root.

Provider keys and preferences live separately in settings.json; DIZEL_CONFIG_DIR overrides that settings location. Back up both roots deliberately, and exclude them from source control when they contain private conversations or credentials.
